consumers’ self-identity is a key driver of brand-related social media behavior.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the symbolic meaning of brands plays an important role in consumers’ brand endorsements, but this role is contingent upon consumers’ self-concept.
consumers’ intention to use social media to signal their identity is driven by their need to belong to a social group, rather than by their need to express a personal identity.
consumers’ endorsement intention is not only determined by their attitudes towards brands and the social media platform, but also by their identity.
